title: Problem Statement: Covering Groups by Abelian Subgroups
content:
Erdős Problem #117 asks: let $h(n)$ be the minimum number of Abelian subgroups needed to cover any group $G$ with the property that every subset of size $> n$ contains two distinct commuting elements. Estimate $h(n)$.

Pyber (1987) proved $c_1^n < h(n) < c_2^n$ for constants $c_2 > c_1 > 1$, establishing exponential growth. The problem remains open — determining the optimal base of the exponential is unknown.
mathContext: $h(n)$: min Abelian subgroups to cover any $G$ with the $n$-commuting property. Known: $c_1^n < h(n) < c_2^n$ (Pyber 1987).

title: n-Commuting Property
content: **HasNCommutingProperty G n**: A group $G$ has the $n$-commuting property if every subset $S \subseteq G$ with $|S| > n$ contains two distinct elements $x \neq y$ with $xy = yx$. This is a Ramsey-type condition: large enough subsets are forced to contain commuting pairs. An Abelian group satisfies this for all $n$, while for non-Abelian groups the minimum such $n$ measures the degree of non-commutativity.
mathContext: $\forall S \subseteq G,\; |S| > n \Rightarrow \exists x \neq y \in S,\; xy = yx$

title: Abelian Subgroup
content: **IsAbelianSubgroup G H**: A subgroup $H \leq G$ is Abelian if all pairs of elements in $H$ commute: $\forall x, y \in H, xy = yx$. This is defined directly via pairwise commutativity rather than using Mathlib's `CommGroup` typeclass, since we need it as a property of a specific subgroup within a non-Abelian ambient group.
mathContext: $H \leq G$ is Abelian $\iff \forall x, y \in H,\; xy = yx$

title: Abelian Cover Number h(n)
content: **abelianCoverNumber n**: The minimum $k$ such that every finite group $G$ with the $n$-commuting property can be covered by $k$ Abelian subgroups: $G = H_1 \cup \cdots \cup H_k$ with each $H_i$ Abelian. Defined as $\inf\{k \in \mathbb{N} : \forall G \text{ finite with } n\text{-commuting}, \exists H_1, \ldots, H_k \text{ Abelian covering } G\}$ via `sInf`. The function is noncomputable due to the universal quantification over all types.
mathContext: $h(n) = \inf\{k : \forall G \text{ finite with } n\text{-commuting property}, G = \bigcup_{i=1}^k H_i,\; H_i \text{ Abelian}\}$

title: Erdős Problem #117: Exponential Bounds
content: **erdos_117_problem**: The main problem statement axiomatizes that $h(n)$ grows exponentially. There exist constants $c_2 > c_1 > 1$ such that $c_1^n < h(n) < c_2^n$ for all $n > 0$. The strict inequalities distinguish this from Pyber's bounds (which use $\leq$). This captures both Pyber's result and the open question of narrowing the gap between the constants.
mathContext: $\exists c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R},\; 1 < c_1 < c_2 : \forall n > 0,\; c_1^n < h(n) < c_2^n$

title: Pyber's Exponential Bounds (1987)
content: **pyber_1987**: Pyber proved that the Abelian covering number is exponential: there exist constants $c_2 > c_1 > 1$ with $c_1^n \leq h(n) \leq c_2^n$ for all $n > 0$. The upper bound constructs Abelian covers using the structure theory of nilpotent groups: a group with the $n$-commuting property has a subgroup of bounded index that is nilpotent of bounded class, and nilpotent groups can be covered by $O(c^n)$ Abelian subgroups. The lower bound exhibits explicit groups (related to wreath products) requiring exponentially many Abelian subgroups.
mathContext: $\exists c_2 > c_1 > 1 : \forall n > 0,\; c_1^n \leq h(n) \leq c_2^n$
